title: Thiriet by TDS wins at Imola as Jota fades
dek: Pierre Thiriet and Mathias Beche won the 3 Hours of Imola for Thiriet by TDS Racing, 46 seconds clear of Signatech Alpine, after pole-sitting Jota's Zytek faded from the lead.

chapters.title: Round two after a washed-out opener
text: The 3 Hours of Imola on 18 May 2013 was the second round of a European Le Mans Series that had opened a month earlier in a deluge. At Silverstone the race was abandoned with 75 per cent of the distance run, 2 hours 15 minutes of a scheduled three, after chaotic tyre calls, a closed pit lane under the new three-lap Safety Car rule and a procession of spins. Jota Sport's Simon Dolan and Oliver Turvey took the LMP2 win from Race Performance, with Thiriet by TDS Racing third after a driver change under the Safety Car that handed Jota the lead back. Murphy Prototypes lost seven laps in one long stop, and Morand Racing was out of the race before Natacha Gachnang had even got in.

Imola brought 28 cars, up from 23 at Silverstone, and a ten-car LMP2 class. HVM Status GP joined with its Lola coupe for Jonathan Hirschi and Tony Burgess, as a lead-in to Le Mans. Hirschi had been third at Silverstone with Thiriet by TDS, which now welcomed back Mathias Beche, the reigning ELMS champion alongside Pierre Thiriet, for his first start of the season in the team's Oreca. Greaves Motorsport swapped its Silverstone line-up for Tom Kimber-Smith and David Heinemeier Hansson, the latter adding an ELMS outing to his full season in another series.

Practice was split by the weather. Friday morning was wet enough for intermediates and a late dry line, with Hirschi's Lola beaching in the Villeneuve gravel and bringing out a four-minute red flag. The afternoon was dry and far more representative: Burgess put the same Lola into the gravel at Rivazza, and Patric Niederhauser and Heinemeier Hansson both spun under braking for Acque Minerale.

chapters.title: Turvey lifts pole by more than half a second
text: Turvey put the Jota Zytek on pole with 1:34.343, his second pole in two rounds, after the prototype session built slowly: the big names left their runs late, and Matthieu Lecuyer's spin just before the line in the LMPC ranks put that stretch of track under yellow flags for several minutes. Beche had been the early pace-setter in the TDS Oreca on a 1:35.5, with Kimber-Smith and Frank Mailleux next, before Turvey took over the top with a 1:35.162 in the final ten minutes, then a 1:34.574 and finally the 1:34.343. He was on a still quicker lap when he saw the gap, lifted and came in. He said afterwards that he had had only five laps in Friday's dry session and was on tyres that had done just three pushing laps.

Beche's 1:34.914 held second, with Brendon Hartley's Murphy Oreca third on 1:34.951, only 37 thousandths short of a second front-row slot. Nelson Panciatici spun the Signatech Alpine through 360 degrees in the final minutes but still improved to 1:35.538, retaking fourth from Kimber-Smith's Greaves Zytek on 1:35.606. Mailleux and Niederhauser were sixth and seventh for Morand and Race Performance, with Hirschi's Lola eighth in class on 1:37.309 and the Boutsen Ginion Oreca of Bastien Brière ninth. DKR Engineering's old Lola was a distant tenth.

chapters.title: Six cars nose to tail
text: The start was clean in dry, bright conditions. Hartley slotted the Murphy Oreca onto the tail of Turvey's Jota and demoted Beche to third, while Mailleux moved the Morand Morgan up to fifth at Kimber-Smith's expense. Hirschi made a poor start in the Lola and was swamped by the leading GT cars. For the first 45 minutes there was little side-by-side passing but constant pressure: the top six were within ten seconds after half an hour, the top five within six, trading fastest laps as the traffic began after about 15 minutes.

The pit stops reshuffled the order. Panciatici handed the Signatech Alpine to Pierre Ragues at around 41 minutes, and on the next lap the leading trio all came in together. Hartley gave way to Mark Patterson while Turvey and Beche stayed aboard. TDS had the quicker stop and Beche came out ahead, with Jota second. But the Murphy Oreca would not restart, a starter motor problem that struck again at each subsequent stop and killed Patterson's chances. Signatech also lost time with starting problems, around half a minute, and fell behind the Greaves car, while Mailleux, who stayed out longest, rejoined third.

chapters.title: Thiriet passes Dolan, Jota unravels
text: Turvey kept chipping at Beche's lead, down to two seconds by half distance, with both setting the fastest laps of the race so far. At the halfway stops Thiriet took over the TDS Oreca and Dolan the Jota. TDS again had the quicker stop, but Thiriet's out-lap was slower and Dolan emerged in front. He held the Frenchman off until Thiriet put a decisive move on him into Tosa, both cars ducking out to pass traffic, and TDS began to pull away.

From there Jota came apart: Dolan spun, and the Zytek began to lose its electrical systems. Gachnang had taken over the Morand Morgan at the halfway point, a step on from Silverstone, but could not resist Heinemeier Hansson, who passed her at Tosa. The Dane then came up behind the Signatech Alpine, whose driver was struggling to get heat into cold tyres after a slow exit from the pits, and passed Panciatici easily.

chapters.title: A stop-and-go reshapes the podium
text: Heinemeier Hansson had crossed the white line at the pit exit to make that pass on the Alpine, and the Greaves car was given a one-minute stop-and-go late in the race. That dropped it from the front group to fifth and promoted Signatech to an uncontested second place. Morand Racing inherited third, one lap behind the top two, despite a late splash-and-dash. Michel Frey and Niederhauser took fourth for Race Performance, ahead of the recovering Greaves car, with the Murphy Oreca of Hartley and Patterson sixth, three laps down.

Thiriet and Beche took the flag after 3:00:13.017 and 108 laps, 46.236 seconds clear of Signatech Alpine. Hartley, who had closed to within two seconds of the stricken Jota before it faded, said he thought Murphy had the pace for the podium without the starter trouble. Dolan and Turvey were not classified on 101 laps: the Zytek, which had been losing electrical systems, stopped on the circuit in the final minutes with an alternator failure. Turvey's 1:34.992 was the fastest lap of the race.

chapters.title: TDS strengthens its hand, Signatech and Morand climb
text: Thiriet by TDS Racing had turned Silverstone's third place into a win, and a fitting return for Beche. He praised Thiriet's stint against Dolan, said the Oreca was slow on the straights but better than the traffic in the corners, and hoped the result would let Thiriet fight for the championship.

Signatech Alpine had the day's best argument for what might have been. Ragues reckoned that without the starter trouble the Alpine would have been 17 seconds off the leader, and probably much closer given the time lost behind Greaves, and said it might have been fighting for the win. Panciatici, who said the car's pace over the long double stint was there, was happy to take the podium and pronounced the team ready for Le Mans. Morand Racing, whose Gachnang said she had not known she was third until ten minutes from the end, will line up Olivier Lombard at Le Mans.

For Murphy Prototypes the lesson was drawn quickly: Hartley said it was better to have the starter problem at Imola than at Le Mans, where Karun Chandhok will join the car. Jota left Italy with a pole and a lead that evaporated, its Silverstone winners not classified, while Greaves had lost a podium to a white-line infringement at the pit exit.
The ELMS now broke for the Le Mans 24 Hours on 22–23 June. The next round was the 3 Hours of the Red Bull Ring in Austria on 20 July.

facts.v: Oliver Turvey's 1:34.343 in the Jota Zytek was more than half a second clear of Mathias Beche's TDS Oreca on 1:34.914.

facts.t: Starter trouble for Murphy and Signatech
facts.v: Murphy Prototypes had a starter motor problem at every stop, and Signatech Alpine lost about half a minute with a starting problem at a stop.
Greaves was handed a one-minute stop-and-go for a pit-exit infringement, which gave second place to Signatech Alpine and third to Morand Racing.

facts.v: The leading Jota Zytek was not classified after stopping on the circuit with alternator failure.
The winners covered 108 laps, 530.17 km, in the first of the ELMS's Imola races, then a three-hour event.
